analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and added-file metadata. UpdateRollback.swift:63-99 adds operator-confirmed predecessor rollback, initial cluster/foreground refusals, an update lease, a post-prompt provider-state check, and restart even after rollback failure. Lines 119-121 await fresh authorization after successful restart; live wiring at 153-171 delegates drain, stop, restart and watchdog rearming. No plaintext, key, billing, cache-format or serving-authorization bypass is established by this wrapper. Relevant contracts are T-043/T-013 (recovery authority and artifact integrity), T-053/T-054 (fresh connection authorization and revoked builds), T-047 (helper lease lifecycle), and A-018 (availability). Rollback alone does not prove any historical cache or encryption regression under T-041/T-008.
UpdateRollbackCommandTests.swift:110-148 tests tampered-predecessor refusal and provider changes during confirmation; its host only records lifecycle events (248-262). UpdateRollbackEndToEndTests.swift:79-149 checks bundle restoration and quarantine using the same built executable under different bundle labels, with fake lifecycle callbacks and signature enforcement disabled in the updater. Its separate ad-hoc codesign verification does not establish production signer qualification. Test-only HTTP and disabled signature checks are not production regressions.
Integration must verify SelfUpdater.rollbackPlan/rollBackToPredecessor revalidate the confirmed plan and artifact under the lease and recover a complete layout on failure (wrapper line 92); ServiceDrain.prepare must fence admission and concurrent starts before swapping, including cluster-state changes after the initial check (64, 82-91). Also verify live restart authorization, production updater configuration, and fan-helper cleanup. These controls are delegated outside supplied evidence, not observed missing controls; no supported finding in this scope.
